To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the children of immigrants face the struggle between two cultures, one represented by their national identity and the other by their family identity, and that the educational system represents the structure of the reproduction of national cultural identity.

the educational system in the receiving country is the most important factor in the development of national identity of the second generation immigrants, and the family environment is the most important for the cultural identity of their country of origin.

globalization has restructured relationships and dependencies between countries around the world, creating systematic dependencies that drive international migration and the creation of immigrant communities outside of countries of origin, and the educational systems of receiving countries are structures of reproduction for the cultural identity of those countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects that the educational system has on the national identity of the second generation immigrants.
the role that education plays in the development of a national and familial cultural identification of immigrant children, specifically the second generation immigrants.
understanding the role of education in second generation immigrants and its impact on national identity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the educational system represents the most significant structure for the reproduction of national cultural identity in second generation immigrants.

the children of immigrants in the educational system face a struggle of national and familial identity, which is a result of the globalization process, but one that can be overcome by the recognition of the importance of the educational system in the process.

the educational systems of the receiving countries are not prepared for the challenges that the children of immigrants face, and that the educational system is not a neutral structure of reproduction, rather, it is a structure of social and cultural reproduction of the receiving country.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified that the educational system in the US, as in many other receiving countries, is not equipped to deal with the needs of immigrant children, especially in the area of cultural identity.
education has the potential to act as a bridge between cultures and as a tool to help immigrants and their children adapt to the new culture.
we have found that the education system has the ability to be a tool to help the immigrant child develop a positive sense of identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a more globalized education system that recognizes the cultural identities of the students and allows them to express their own identity in their educational experience.
the educational system must be reformed to accommodate the needs of the immigrant population, and that the educational system can be a place of cultural identity formation.
education is the key to a successful transition into the receiving country for second generation immigrants, and it should be used as a tool to facilitate this integration.
